recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. No core source edit is needed for FHIR-11303; future work should only revisit this if OO changes the post-FHIR-17540 policy that infant body length is represented as a more specific coding under the Body height vital-sign profile.
issue_request: FHIR-11303 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core OO change request from the DSTU2 vital-signs page asking that infant height use the clinically appropriate body length / Body height lying down terminology, with the resolution to add this in alignment with US Core Vital Signs.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-11303. The closest application trail is the 2016-11-04 US Core/vitals alignment commit 0ae70da2, immediately after the 2016-11-03 vote, which retained/additionally wired Body length / 8306-3 material in the vital-signs profile. Earlier draft source already contained 8306-3, so this issue appears to have confirmed and retained body length handling rather than introducing it from nothing.
additional_context: FHIR-13801 later questioned the separate Body length profile and documented the translation/additional-coding discussion, but was resolved No Change because pediatric body length remained clinically relevant. FHIR-17540 then made the later published change to remove the separate Body length line/profile treatment and include 8306-3 Body height - lying under Body height as an additional Observation.code coding. OO minutes from 2018-07-26 record the same remove-body-length/add-to-body-height decision. FHIR-32787 later clarified vital-signs table wording and preserved the body-length guidance as a more specific Observation.code coding.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/fhir.ini keeps Observation in build scope; the Observation vital-signs IG references StructureDefinition/bodyheight; the Body Height profile summary and binding description include body length; the vital-signs narrative says 8306-3 Body height - lying/body length may be used in Observation.code; and the body-length example includes both 8306-3 and the general 8302-2 Body height coding.
